scenario.title: Alstom Transport UK Ltd v London Underground Ltd
scenario.description: London Underground awarded contract to Bombardier for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment. Alstom challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. The challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. London Underground applied to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework, arguing that damages would be adequate remedy for Alstom if it succeeded at trial and that the balance of convenience favoured proceeding with the contract.

interests: Protection of Public Funds: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Critical infrastructure and transportation services may be disrupted if the contract is delayed or re-run
Reputation & Public Accountability: London Underground's reputation as a competent, fair and professional buyer could be damaged by an adverse outcome
goals: Maintain public confidence in the procurement process
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We will defend our evaluation process, which was conducted fairly and in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Fairness & Transparency: perceived manifest error in technical threshold requirement application
Protection of Reputation: maintain credibility with parent companies, shareholders and partners
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We believe there was a manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. We request that London Underground re-evaluate the bids to ensure fairness and transparency.

messages.message: Alstom Transport UK Ltd has challenged our procurement decision on the grounds of a manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement. We understand that this challenge was brought during the standstill period, which triggered an automatic suspension. However, we would like to clarify whether Alstom is alleging that the evaluation team's interpretation of the technical threshold was incorrect or if there was a procedural flaw in the evaluation process. Could you please provide more information on what specific actions or decisions you believe were manifestly wrong and how this impacted your bid?

Thank you for your clarification request. I'd like to clarify that our challenge is based on a procedural flaw in the evaluation process, specifically regarding the application of the technical threshold requirement. We believe that this was not applied consistently across all bids and that our own bid met the required standard. To address your question directly, we are alleging that there was an error in the evaluation team's interpretation of the technical threshold, which resulted in our bid being unfairly disadvantaged. I'd like to request a detailed explanation of the evaluation process, including any scoring discrepancies or evaluator comments related to this specific requirement.

We acknowledge Alstom's concerns regarding the technical threshold requirement and agree to provide a detailed explanation of the evaluation process, including any scoring discrepancies or evaluator comments related to this specific requirement. However, we must clarify that our evaluation team applied the technical threshold consistently across all bids, as evidenced by the evaluation records. We are willing to share these records with Alstom to demonstrate the transparency and fairness of our procurement process. Furthermore, we would like to propose a voluntary standstill extension for an additional 14 days to allow for further engagement and clarification on this matter.

We appreciate your willingness to share evaluation records and provide a detailed explanation of the evaluation process. However, we would like to request that you also provide specific examples or case studies from the evaluation records that demonstrate how the technical threshold was consistently applied across all bids. This will help us understand the evaluation team's reasoning and assess whether our bid was indeed unfairly disadvantaged. Furthermore, we are willing to accept a voluntary standstill extension for an additional 14 days as proposed by London Underground, but only if it is accompanied by a commitment from both parties to engage in good faith negotiations and work towards a mutually acceptable resolution.

We agree to provide specific examples or case studies from the evaluation records that demonstrate how the technical threshold was consistently applied across all bids. We will also share these records with Alstom to demonstrate the transparency and fairness of our procurement process. Furthermore, we confirm our commitment to engage in good faith negotiations and work towards a mutually acceptable resolution during the proposed 14-day voluntary standstill extension.
messages.proposal: A partial award covering 50% of the contract value, contingent on successful negotiation of the disputed technical threshold requirement
messages.concession_made: Voluntary standstill extension for an additional 14 days

messages.message: We appreciate your commitment to good faith negotiations and transparency in this matter. However, we still require specific examples or case studies from the evaluation records that demonstrate how the technical threshold was consistently applied across all bids. Without these concrete examples, it will be challenging for us to assess whether our bid was unfairly disadvantaged. We propose a compromise: allow an independent expert to review the evaluation process and provide an objective assessment of the technical threshold application. This would not only provide clarity on this matter but also demonstrate London Underground's commitment to fairness and transparency.

We appreciate Alstom's proposal for an independent expert to review the evaluation process and provide an objective assessment of the technical threshold application. We are willing to consider this option, but would like to propose a compromise: instead of bringing in an external expert, we could invite a joint review by both our internal evaluation team and Alstom's representatives. This would allow for a collaborative examination of the evaluation process and provide a more efficient resolution to this matter.

We appreciate London Underground's willingness to consider an independent review of the evaluation process. However, we believe that a joint review by both our internal evaluation team and Alstom's representatives would not provide the same level of objectivity as an external expert. Nevertheless, we are willing to compromise on this point and accept a joint review if it is accompanied by a clear commitment from London Underground to implement any recommended changes to their evaluation process. We also propose that the joint review be facilitated by a neutral third-party chair who can ensure that both parties have an equal opportunity to present their views and contribute to the review process.
messages.proposal: A joint review of the evaluation process, facilitated by a neutral third-party chair

messages.message: We are willing to accept Alstom's proposal for a joint review facilitated by a neutral third-party chair, with a clear commitment from London Underground to implement any recommended changes to our evaluation process. We believe this will provide a fair and transparent resolution to this matter. Furthermore, we propose that the joint review be conducted within the next 14 days, allowing us to lift the automatic suspension and proceed with the contract award.
messages.concession_made: We are willing to commit to implementing any recommended changes to our evaluation process

messages.message: We believe that we have reached a satisfactory agreement on the joint review process and are willing to proceed with it. We propose that the joint review be conducted within the next 14 days, as previously agreed upon. Additionally, we would like to request that London Underground commit to implementing any recommended changes to their evaluation process, as previously proposed by Alstom. This will ensure that our concerns regarding the technical threshold requirement are addressed and provide a fair and transparent resolution to this matter.
messages.concession_made: We are willing to accept the joint review being facilitated by London Underground's internal evaluation team, rather than an independent expert.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome of the negotiation is considered acceptable, as it avoided the costs and risks associated with proceeding to formal proceedings under the Procurement Act 2023. The negotiation process allowed for a more efficient resolution to the dispute, which would have otherwise taken several months and incurred significant legal fees.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We were able to maintain control of the negotiation process and avoid concessions on key issues, such as the evaluation team's interpretation of the technical threshold requirement. We also successfully proposed a joint review facilitated by a neutral third-party chair, which will provide a fair and transparent resolution to this matter.
what_was_achieved: A detailed explanation of the evaluation process was provided to Alstom, including scoring discrepancies and evaluator comments related to the technical threshold requirement.
Specific examples or case studies from the evaluation records were shared with Alstom to demonstrate how the technical threshold was consistently applied across all bids.
A joint review facilitated by a neutral third-party chair will be conducted within the next 14 days, allowing for a fair and transparent resolution to this matter.
what_was_conceded: The automatic suspension triggered by Alstom's challenge during the standstill period was maintained for several rounds of negotiation.
A commitment to implement any recommended changes to our evaluation process was made in order to address Alstom's concerns regarding the technical threshold requirement.

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The negotiation outcome is slightly better than pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings, but not significantly so. While we were able to secure a joint review of the evaluation process and a commitment from London Underground to implement any recommended changes, this does not necessarily mean that our bid will be re-evaluated or that we will ultimately succeed in our challenge.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We have secured a joint review of the evaluation process, which should provide clarity on whether our bid was unfairly disadvantaged. We also obtained a commitment from London Underground to implement any recommended changes to their evaluation process, which demonstrates their willingness to address our concerns and improve their procurement practices.
what_was_achieved: A joint review of the evaluation process will be conducted within the next 14 days
London Underground has committed to implementing any recommended changes to their evaluation process
what_was_conceded: We did not secure an independent external expert review, instead opting for a joint review facilitated by a neutral third-party chair
The negotiation ultimately ended in deadlock, requiring escalation to formal proceedings

key_sticking_points: Application of the technical threshold requirement
Consistency of evaluation process across all bids
Transparency and fairness in procurement process
summary.concessions_summary: Both parties made concessions throughout the negotiation. The Contracting Authority agreed to provide specific examples or case studies from the evaluation records, share evaluation records with Alstom, and commit to implementing any recommended changes to their evaluation process. Alstom accepted a joint review facilitated by London Underground's internal evaluation team instead of an independent expert.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively due to the technical nature of the dispute. The Court found that the Contracting Authority followed the procurement process, but there was no manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement. However, the Court noted that the parties demonstrated a willingness to collaborate and improve the evaluation process.
summary.likely_next_steps: The negotiation reached a deadlock after Round 5, with both parties unable to agree on the terms of the joint review. As a result, the case will likely proceed to formal proceedings, where an independent expert or tribunal will assess the procurement process and determine whether Alstom's bid was unfairly disadvantaged.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation between Alstom Transport UK Ltd and London Underground Ltd centered around a dispute over the application of the technical threshold requirement in the procurement process. Despite concessions made by both parties, they were unable to reach an agreement on the terms of a joint review. As a result, the case will likely proceed to formal proceedings, where an independent expert or tribunal will assess the procurement process and determine whether Alstom's bid was unfairly disadvantaged.
